reviewer_role: fresh independent Phase D implementation auditor
scope: Read-only source and bounded execution audit of the committed Phase D implementation. The reviewer did not edit implementation source and did not use archived Article 3 measurements. Concurrent uncommitted changes to article3/formal/results.json and article3/reviews/theory_review.json were outside this review; every implementation and design file below was hashed from reviewed_head with git show.

summary.reason: Authoritative usage can still be forged by a workload principal, tenant binding is derived from caller-controlled Pod metadata, governed traffic can bypass injection/proxy classification, and the Envoy example does not actuate the deployment selected by admission. Thirteen required production/research mechanisms also remain absent.

prior_finding_reassessment.evidence: validateGOVARConfig now rejects incomplete enabled annotations and the proxy returns 503 for recognized governed paths when runtime configuration is incomplete. However injector.go:206-217 lets a Pod annotation aiops.imperium.io/sidecar-injection=false override namespace enablement; validation only executes inside the enabled branch at injector.go:162-180. No NetworkPolicy or other direct-egress enforcement exists in charts/config.

An official ext_proc gRPC server and mTLS Envoy example now exist and the rendered configuration validates with Envoy v1.31. Nevertheless server.go:265-270 mutates only x-ai-eg-model, while the request JSON model remains unchanged and the example routes every request to one fixed llm_backend cluster at gov-ar-envoy-example-configmap.yaml:42-43,86-96. The lifecycle test asserts only the header mutation. Therefore selected deployment/provider actuation is not demonstrated.

Namespace-bound HMAC derivation, TokenReview Pod UID checks, live Pod lookup, and public authoritative_unbilled denial were added. But trustedWorkloadFromPod at main.go:529-540 treats Pod-authored tenant/team/application/budget/routing annotations as authority. More critically, handleSettle at main.go:304-334 allows any authenticated workload bearer to provide actual_input_tokens, actual_output_tokens, usage_version and final=true; only nonzero actual_cost_micros is forbidden. A governed Pod possessing its projected token can race a zero-token final settlement for its real request and release the residual hold without provider-authoritative usage. In addition, ext_proc authorizes the gateway certificate but resolves downstream identity solely from the stream-supplied XFCC at server.go:65-71,231-250; a direct client holding the allowed gateway identity can select any registered workload URI.

Recognized OpenAI-style LLM paths ignore the Pod target filter and all governed CONNECT requests fail closed. But isGOVARRequest at proxy.go:340-344 is a path substring heuristic that omits common governed shapes such as /v1/messages and generateContent. Combined with Pod-controlled target hosts and injection opt-out, such calls are forwarded without admission.

Only tenant/cohort_id/cohort_index uniqueness exists (postgres_engine.go:144-145 and engine.go:308-313). There is no pre-outcome cohort registry fixing membership, opportunity identities/features, N, weights, alpha_K, source/config hash, or freeze time. Cohort size/risk remain routing annotations and cohort identity/index remain request fields.

routing.Spec.Canary.Enabled always returns REQUIRE_APPROVAL at engine.go:285-287 and postgres_engine.go:230-232. AdmitRequest has no approval reference and the service does not read or consume an approved AIChangeRequest, bind its version, prevent replay, or allow the approved request to re-enter.

Budget identity changes still fail closed when any exposure exists (engine.go:698-705; postgres_engine.go:275-287). MIGRATIONS.md explicitly states automated rollover and carry allocation are not implemented. There are no origin/current window fields, rollover guards, debt payoff, or historical audit-credit records.

VerifiedOutputCap is still a model annotation assertion (snapshot.go:14-18,92-99), and the immutable ledger price snapshot includes only input/output token prices. Cached input, hidden reasoning, tools, media, cancellation, retry/fallback and other provider billable categories/cap semantics are neither typed nor introspected.

Adaptive tokens, support, drift and cohort parameters are read directly from AIRoutingPolicy annotations (admission_policy.go:14-22,173-187). No calibration store, selected-feedback updater, detector, immutable calibration artifact, conservative-mode status producer, or revalidation controller exists.

AIModel, AIProvider and AIRoutingPolicy APIs contain no typed GOV-AR routability, pricing version/freshness, verified cap, latency, calibration, drift, cohort or risk-allocation fields. Safety-critical values remain mutable unvalidated annotations. Generated CRD schemas therefore cannot validate these controls.

govar_outbox and CAS transitions exist, but repository search finds no outbox dispatch worker, expiry compare/cancel worker, unresolved resolver, correction/finality reconciler, or rollover worker. Ext_proc performs synchronous calls and discards dispatch/settlement/cancel errors at server.go:91-107. Downward post-final correction is discarded rather than recorded as immutable origin-window audit credit (engine.go:539-541).

The service exposes the default Prometheus handler at main.go:158, but no GOV-AR counters, histograms, gauges, trace propagation, OpenTelemetry spans, or immutable structured transition audit are registered or emitted.

Both paths buffer full bodies. sidecarproxy uses unbounded io.ReadAll for request and response bodies (proxy.go:195,350), while ext_proc appends all request/response chunks without an application bound (server.go:77,100). The example forces BUFFERED request and response modes; SSE/streaming usage, disconnect, cancellation and terminal settlement semantics are absent.

article3/infra/postgres/init.sql still creates the legacy DOUBLE PRECISION schema, whereas service startup rejects nonempty legacy rows. MIGRATIONS.md documents manual fail-closed handling but provides no conversion tool, reconciliation proof, versioned API compatibility, or tested database upgrade/rollback path.

The parent reported an independently run stable Kind result of 1/1 pass, but no source-hash-bound result/log was present for this reviewer. More importantly, test/e2e/e2e_test.go:79-143 only builds, installs and checks the controller-manager Pod; it does not deploy PostgreSQL or gov-ar-admission, run Envoy ext_proc, reserve, dispatch to the selected backend, extract usage, settle, or verify a ledger. It is not the required GOV-AR Kind path.

new_findings.summary: A workload principal can forge final provider usage and release a live hold.
new_findings.counterexample: After the legitimate gateway claims/delivers request R for the Pod, code running in that same Pod reads the projected GOV-AR token and POSTs /v1/settle for R with actual_input_tokens=0, actual_output_tokens=0, usage_version=1, final=true. TokenReview authenticates the Pod, handleSettle accepts zero cost and caller-supplied token counts, and applySettlement finalizes and releases the residual reservation. No provider or reconciler authority distinguishes this forged event.
new_findings.required_repair: Use role-separated authentication/authorization. Workload identities may request admission but must never post authoritative usage/finality. Accept usage only from an authenticated gateway/provider adapter or reconciler identity, bind it to the immutable provider attempt, and add a regression test for the exact forged zero-token settlement.

new_findings.summary: TokenReview proves the Pod but not its tenant/governance assignment.
new_findings.counterexample: A principal permitted to create its Pod chooses govar-tenant, team, application, budget-policy, routing-policy, sensitivity and zones annotations. The webhook copies them and the admission server later calls the live Pod metadata authoritative. The Pod can therefore target another tenant/budget unless a separate admission/RBAC policy outside this implementation happens to forbid those annotations.
new_findings.required_repair: Resolve tenant and governance policy from operator-owned, immutable or admission-validated Namespace/workload registry state that Pod creators cannot select. Bind Pod UID/resourceVersion to that record and test cross-tenant Pod-annotation claims.

new_findings.summary: The native Envoy path does not dispatch to the deployment selected by admission.
new_findings.counterexample: The client sends model=original. Admission returns model-eu. ext_proc adds only x-ai-eg-model=model-eu, then Envoy routes to the same fixed llm_backend and forwards the unchanged JSON body. A normal OpenAI/Azure provider therefore receives original or a fixed deployment rather than the selected route.
new_findings.required_repair: Implement and test actual route/backend and provider-deployment actuation compatible with the target gateway (including deployment URL/body semantics), and verify the selected deployment received the request in a real Envoy/PostgreSQL/backend E2E test.

new_findings.summary: Governed workloads can bypass the measured admission path.
new_findings.counterexample: A Pod overrides namespace injection with sidecar-injection=false, unsets proxy environment variables, opens a direct socket, or calls an omitted provider path such as /v1/messages while excluding the host from target-hosts. No chart NetworkPolicy forces LLM egress through the gateway.
new_findings.required_repair: Make governance assignment non-overridable by Pods, force governed egress through the authenticated gateway within the declared trust boundary, and classify/routably bind providers rather than relying on path substrings. Add bypass-negative E2E tests.

new_findings.summary: The allowed gateway mTLS identity is not cryptographically bound to the downstream XFCC identity.
new_findings.evidence: authorizeGatewayTransport validates only the ext_proc client certificate URI. resolvePrincipal separately trusts x-forwarded-client-cert supplied on the gRPC stream. Tests reject no certificate and an unapproved gateway certificate, but do not send a forged registered XFCC using the approved gateway certificate. SANITIZE_SET is a correct deployment control in the example, but the ext_proc service itself cannot distinguish compliant Envoy from a direct holder of that credential.
new_findings.required_repair: Use a channel/metadata binding that the allowed gateway cannot arbitrarily author, narrow credential possession and authorization, or explicitly scope this as trusted-gateway behavior with a conformance control and exact approved-certificate spoof regression.

new_findings.summary: The GOV-AR Dockerfile builds but its source-stage image references are mutable tags.
new_findings.evidence: Dockerfile.gov-ar-admission uses golang:1.21 and gcr.io/distroless/static:nonroot rather than immutable source digests. This review's local build resolved concrete digests, but later clean builds need not resolve the same bytes.
new_findings.required_repair: Pin build and runtime images by digest, record build platform/toolchain, and verify the image digest in the clean release build.

minor_findings.summary: Policy and quality freshness checks accept timestamps arbitrarily far in the future because time.Since is checked without a corresponding future bound; pricing/latency do include a one-minute future guard.
HTTP authentication reads at most 1 MiB but does not explicitly reject an over-limit body; a complete JSON prefix can be authenticated while trailing bytes are silently unread.
The Helm Envoy example validates but emits Envoy's warning that internal_address_config is unspecified. This is not the reason for the failed verdict.
